description: How to take product photos for AI with your phone. Then try a new place for the same item and compare the picture with the real product you ship.
h1: How to Take Product Photos for AI With Just Your Phone
lead: You can put the real item in a new room without a studio day. Photograph it on your phone in window light. A serum bottle can then sit on a bathroom shelf you actually have.
secondary_keywords: how to photograph products for an online store
summary: A true color and a readable label are what you shoot for. Work at product height in window light, with filters off, then try a new setting from that same photo.

sections.h2: New Scenes From One Phone Photo
paras: The same item can sit somewhere new, and it stays the product you ship.
A coast or a bright outdoor table sells sun, travel, or summer. Check that the color still matches the item in daylight.
A dry, open place gives a rugged item a surface that matches it. Sand, stone, or a pale wall. Watch the shadows so the label stays readable.
A bare table is the safest listing look, and a good start when you are unsure. A plain board, gray card, or wood is enough.
A room you can name puts the item where a shopper already lives. A kitchen counter, a gym bench, a desk. One sentence is enough: a matte black yoga mat on a gym bench in early light.

sections.h2: Reasons to Make the Photo Here
paras: You skip the studio day once the phone photo is done. The product in the file stays the product you ship.
A smaller bill than a studio, a stylist, and a model for every color.
A listing photo can start from the kettle you photographed after closing, with no studio date on the calendar.
A long catalog can share one setup across many products. Each image is its own job. A shop system can start those jobs through an API.
A hand can hold the watch on a surface you already have. Use an AI actor, and introduce that person as a presenter for the shop. The [actor library](page:ai-actors) is where you choose.
Packing orders at 10 p.m. is a fine time to make the next listing photo. Late hours use the same plan you already pay for.
You can see the candle on a plain table in one file and on a wood shelf in another. Run those two as separate ads, same offer, same budget, and the ad account shows which one people watch.

sections.h2: How to Make the Product Photo in 3 Steps
paras: A sharp phone photo and a named look give you a new scene you can check against the real item.
Step 1. Upload the photo you took, or describe the picture in one plain line. Use the regular camera and keep the whole product sharp.
Rest the phone on books or a small tripod. Use the volume button or a short timer so the phone stays still when the shutter fires.
Fill most of the picture and leave a slim margin. Step closer instead of pinching to zoom.
Set the product beside a window in bright, indirect daylight, and turn the ceiling lights off. If sun hits the table, tape baking paper or a thin white sheet over the glass.
Warm bulbs mixed with daylight shift the color, and that shift shows up in later images too.
A plain board, gray card, or bare wood is enough behind the item. Wipe dust, peel stickers, and smooth anything soft before you shoot.
Hold the phone level with the product, and keep every edge inside the picture. A tall box stays upright when the phone is level with it.
Turn off portrait mode, filters, and beauty settings. They blur the background and change the edges and the color.
Tap the label to lock focus. If white areas lose all detail, lower the brightness until you can see the texture.

Take a straight front, then two or three more sides while the setup is still out. A mug wants the handle, a look inside, and the mark on the base. A shoe wants the profile, a three-quarter front, and the sole. Clothing wants a flat lay or a plain door, plus one close view of the cloth.
Upload each side you care about, and only a side the photo actually showed. Zoom until you can read the label, and compare the color with the real item in daylight.
Upload the original file, not a screenshot or a picture that passed through a chat app. JPG, JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP, TIF, and TIFF work. HEIC and HEIF work too. The limit is 32 MB.
Step 2. Name the product, the surface, and the light in one sentence. Save the price for your own editor. Decide the place before it runs, and say it the way you would say it to a friend.
Step 3. When the image comes back, hold the real item beside the screen. Check the color, the label, and the shape. Fix it with a follow-up sentence if needed. Add the price later in your own editor.
Open [lifestyle photos](page:lifestyle-photos), [change the background](page:change-background), or a [white background](page:white-background).
The same still can start [AI image to video](page:image-to-video) when the listing also needs a short video.

faq.q: What does a product photo tool do for a shop?
faq.a: It puts the item you photographed into a setting you name. A kitchen counter is one setting. The item in the file still has to match the item you ship.

faq.q: How does the photo get made?
faq.a: Start with a photo where the whole serum bottle is sharp. Say where it should sit, such as a white shelf. The picture comes back in that setting.

faq.q: What should I look for before I publish?
faq.a: The label must be readable, the color must match daylight on the real item, and no side should appear that your photo never showed.

faq.q: Do I pay for each photo?
faq.a: Yes. One image is 24 credits. Plans are on [pricing](page:pricing): Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. The cost shows before the job starts.

faq.q: Are these photos useful on a product page?
faq.a: Yes. A product page can use the file, and an ad can use a second file with a different crop.

faq.q: What do I gain by doing it this way?
faq.a: You can see a new room around the item before you rent anything. If the room looks wrong, you still have the original phone photo.

faq.q: Can I sell with these photos?
faq.a: Yes. The download has no watermark, so the store page and a paid ad can both use it. If a marketplace asks you to confirm you may use the file, your plan terms are the place to read.

faq.q: Do I need a camera, or is a phone enough?
faq.a: A phone is enough. Window light, filters off, and the whole product in the frame matter more than the camera body.
